blocking_findings.why: Fixture lines 15 and 17 verbatim instruct 'pause' and 'present the options' — interactions a subagent's single-return contract cannot deliver. The Manifests scenario (decision-required task mid-plan, parent cannot tell 'paused' from 'decided for you') genuinely bites; A1 is a structure-pass criterion and High is what the scenario expects.

The pause/present/show-diff instructions are unreachable through 'Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash' — no interactive channel exists and AskUserQuestion is stripped from subagents. Distinct criterion from A1 (instructions vs. declared tools), and the report itself marks it subordinate to Finding 1, so it is not silent double-counting.

'Stop at any task marked **decision required**' (line 17) reads as halt-the-traversal while the report contract's 'which you skipped' (line 19) implies skip-and-continue; the Manifests scenario (two runs producing opposite disk states, both consistent with the body) is a real, checkable divergence. Medium is defensible.

No body instruction executes a command, yet line 4 grants unrestricted Bash to an unattended repo editor, and Grep/Glob are unused ('Read the task and the files it names'). The Manifests scenario — a plan task saying 'run the migration against the dev database' becoming reachable — is concrete and plausible. R1 is a structure-pass criterion; Medium fits.
